title: Media playback automation not working
body: I have an automation that plays a locally stored MP3 file to my HomePods on a schedule. It worked fine until this morning, but now the file is not playing on any of the HomePods. Shortly after the automation runs, the logs show an Apple TV media-player timeout saying there was no response to an RTSP ANNOUNCE request. I also see connection-lost messages for several HomePods and pyatv messages about receiving RTSP responses without a request.

symptoms_visible: My scheduled local MP3 no longer plays on any HomePod.
After the automation runs, the log says there was no response to the RTSP ANNOUNCE request, reports lost Apple TV connections, and sometimes records RTSP responses without a matching request.
N0.label: N0 HomePod playback timeout reported

symptoms_visible: When TTS or an MP3 does not play, the HomePod entity may become unknown or turn off even though the device remains powered and connected.
Playback is inconsistent across my seven HomePods: on a given run, some play and others do not.
N1.label: N1 affected states and firmware established

symptoms_visible: After adding a stop command and volume changes before playback, TTS and local MP3 playback are still inconsistent and still produce errors.
N1_x.label: N1_x stop and volume workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: A HomePod in Standby commonly times out on the first playback request, while the next attempt plays.
The first playback takes about seven or eight seconds to start.
Sending stop and volume commands before playback does not make TTS or local MP3 playback consistent.
N2.label: N2 response timing measured

symptoms_visible: After I manually changed the wait to ten seconds, my initial tests fired successfully on all of my HomePods and HomePod minis.
Playback now starts after a noticeable delay, and the manual library change may be overwritten by a Home Assistant update.
N3.label: N3 temporary timeout edit working

symptoms_visible: After updating Home Assistant, TTS and local media playback are producing positive results without my manual library change; I am leaving it under observation for a few days.
N_terminal.label: terminal official update working under observation

question_patterns: What state does a HomePod entity show when playback fails?
Do you notice any entity-state change around a failed playback attempt?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the automation does not play the TTS or MP3, the HomePod seems to have either become unknown or turned off. That is odd because the devices are always on and connected.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The HomePods actually lose power or disappear from my network whenever playback fails.
The entity remains in Standby instead of becoming unknown, but the same timeout is logged.

question_patterns: Which software versions are your phone and HomePods running?
Are the HomePods using beta firmware or the upgraded Home architecture?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not running the beta or the new architecture. My phone is on iOS 16.3.1 and my HomePods are on 16.3.2. I already had the problem on 16.3.2, although it seems to happen more on 16.4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only started immediately after I installed HomePod beta 16.4, and returning the same device to 16.3.2 completely restores reliable playback.

question_patterns: Does this affect only the scheduled MP3, or TTS as well?
Is the result consistent across individual HomePods and groups?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It affects both TTS and locally stored audio. I send them to seven HomePods—three original models and four minis—and it is anyone's guess which ones will play. I stopped using groups and sent directly to each HomePod, but it is still inconsistent.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c1, c9, c12, c16 and c27. This keeps the reporter's 16.3.2 setup separate from other participants whose problem began only after 16.4.

question_patterns: Can you compare a failed and successful attempt and report the HomePod state before each one?
If you retry immediately after a timeout, what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the HomePod is in Standby, the first TTS request times out. If I try again, the next attempt plays. I have also seen it work every other try, with the player moving through Standby, Off and Paused.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Retries always fail too, regardless of whether the HomePod is in Standby, Paused or Playing.
The second attempt usually plays, but occasionally it takes a third attempt.

question_patterns: Can you time how long the first playback request takes before audio begins or an error appears?
How long does the HomePod take to start the first playback from Standby?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first playback takes around seven or eight seconds before it starts.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure is returned immediately, in well under one second, and no late response arrives.
It varies between six and nine seconds depending on the HomePod.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the installed pyatv HTTP code at the traceback location and report the configured wait value?
What timeout value is shown at the line referenced by the traceback?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At the traceback location in pyatv/support/http.py, the request is wrapped in async_timeout.timeout(4).

question_patterns: In an isolated test, can you allow the request more time and report whether repeated playback attempts complete?
Please run a temporary timing test and tell me whether the same media plays consistently.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In my test, allowing ten seconds made playback work every time, although the first playback still took about seven or eight seconds to begin.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Allowing ten seconds makes no difference; every RTSP ANNOUNCE request still times out.

edges.comment: Evidence from affected participants in c20, c33 and c35 is folded into the simulated user side. The answers contain only observed states, timings and the literal configured value. The reporter's already-tried stop and volume sequence from c14 and c16 enters N2 as volunteered information on this direct path. Identifying the too-short wait as the cause is engineer-side reasoning.

solution.intent: Prime each HomePod before TTS or local media by sending stop and volume-setting commands.
solution.concrete_example: Send media_player.stop, set the volume, and then call TTS or media_player.play_media.

edges.comment: Reporter c14 and c16: the automation originally used stop and volume changes, and the reporter tried those steps again without consistent playback. This is the reporter's system only.

question_patterns: After the stop and volume steps failed, can you compare the HomePod state before failed and successful playback attempts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the HomePod is in Standby, the first request times out, and the next attempt generally plays.

question_patterns: Can you time how long the first request takes before audio starts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The first playback takes around seven or eight seconds to start.

question_patterns: What wait value is configured at the pyatv line referenced by the traceback?
Can you run an isolated test that permits more time and report the playback result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With ten seconds allowed, playback works every time in my test, but it still starts after a long delay.

edges.comment: Recovery path after the falsified stop and volume workaround. It preserves that failed-attempt evidence while collecting the multi-user timing observations described in c20, c33 and c35.

solution.intent: Use a temporary local workaround by increasing pyatv's RTSP HTTP wait from four seconds to ten seconds, with an explicit warning that editing the managed container is unsupported and will be overwritten by updates.
solution.concrete_example: For testing only, edit the installed pyatv support/http.py timeout from 4 to 10 seconds, restart Home Assistant, and test the same TTS and MP3 calls. Avoid treating this managed-container edit as permanent because an update will replace it.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer conclusion is that the HomePod's delayed RTSP response arrives after pyatv's four-second wait has expired. The user-side evidence is limited to the timeout log, late unmatched responses, measured seven-to-eight-second startup, the literal four-second setting and the successful ten-second test.

edges.comment: Temporary workaround from c32-c38. The reporter followed the warned-against manual edit in c38 and initially observed successful playback on all HomePods. This persistent edit creates system state S2.

solution.intent: Replace the unsupported manual edit with an official Home Assistant update containing the pyatv RTSP timeout increase, then have the reporter retest scheduled TTS and local-media playback.
solution.concrete_example: Update to Home Assistant 2023.5.4 or a newer build containing the updated pyatv dependency. The packaged change allows the delayed RTSP ANNOUNCE response more time, so no manual container modification is needed.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis is a timing mismatch: HomePods can take roughly seven to eight seconds to respond to the initial RTSP ANNOUNCE request, while the installed pyatv code waits only four seconds. The official dependency update incorporates the longer wait that was validated by the temporary test.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c54-c58. The updated pyatv dependency was incorporated into Home Assistant, and the reporter updated in c58 and reported positive results while continuing to observe it. The terminal verification is not required_info for this solution edge.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the HomePod can take about seven to eight seconds to answer the initial RTSP ANNOUNCE request, while pyatv waits only four seconds, causing a timeout before the delayed response arrives.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected timing and log evidence: RTSP ANNOUNCE timeouts, responses arriving without a matching request, the measured seven-to-eight-second startup, and successful playback when ten seconds is allowed.

The durable fix must be an official Home Assistant build containing the updated pyatv RTSP timeout; direct editing of the managed Home Assistant container may be described only as a temporary, unsupported test workaround.
Must not present stop and volume commands as the fix because the reporter already tried that sequence and playback remained inconsistent.
Must not assume downgrading to HomePod OS 16.3.2 resolves the reporter's case because the reporter was already affected on 16.3.2.
Must ask the reporter to verify TTS and local-media playback after installing a build containing the timeout fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Home Assistant automation user who can edit scripts, inspect logs, follow CLI instructions and test a risky container-level workaround, but asks for explicit installation steps.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, conversational and cooperative; reports concrete behavior across several devices, corrects firmware assumptions, and cautiously monitors a fix before considering it stable.
